references.text: The naming of Jacob, where his name is linked to 'heel holder' (עָקֵב). Esau plays on this name in 27:36 when he says, 'Is that why he is called Jacob?' and accuses him of having deceived him twice.
Describes how Jacob bought Esau's birthright, which is the first event Esau refers to when he says, 'He took my birthright.'
Tells the story of how Jacob received the blessing that Isaac had intended for Esau, which is the second event Esau refers to when he says, 'Now he has taken my blessing.'
Hosea refers to Jacob deceiving his brother, connecting to Esau's accusation and the wordplay on the name Jacob.

Warns against immorality and godlessness by using Esau as an example, who sold his birthright for a single meal and later found no opportunity for repentance even though he sought the blessing with tears.
This verse describes the actual act of deception that Esau refers to when he says Jacob has deceived him twice.
Malachi interprets Esau's loss of the blessing and birthright as a manifestation of God's eternal choice of Jacob.
Describes the first deception (the sale of the birthright) that Esau refers to when he says he was deceived twice.
Is part of the first event (the sale of the birthright) that Esau refers to in his complaint.
